kv_head_replication.note: What the LOADER applies above one rank, published since v29 because a world above 1 is now attested (tessera#330). vLLM's QKVParallelLinear sets num_kv_head_replicas = tp_size // total_num_kv_heads (at least 1) and its weight_loader gives rank tp_rank the k and v shard at tp_rank // num_kv_head_replicas; tessera.serving.sharding.layer_replicas reads the attribute off the layer and plans each rank's rows from it. The validator checks attribute and shard_index against sharding.KV_REPLICAS_ATTRIBUTE, the constant the loader reads, exactly as loader_axes is checked against ROUTE_TP_AXES. exercised_by_receipt is false: the world-size receipt's model declares 64 key/value heads, so a world of two replicates nothing, and no attention module in it is a Tessera module.

tensor_parallel.units_note: max_world_size is an ATTESTATION bound: the largest tensor-parallel world size a served receipt covers. A unit at 1 names nothing. A unit above 1 names a world_size_receipts entry at exactly that world, and the validator refuses it by name without one: the entry carries each serve's record (image, tree, hosts, flags asking for that world), one route trace per rank, the units those traces executed, the KL against a single-rank arm (a quantized arm, a no-Tessera control and a single-rank floor, with the excess over the control derived from the metrics) and the grade, which is route_only because the KL compares a checkpoint with itself at another world and never with its reference. Since v29 every declared family is at 2 on the GLM-5.3-Flash 4-layer stub serves (docs/measurements/tessera-glm53-a4-stub-tp2-world-size-2026-09-15.md): all three routes executed on both ranks of both two-rank serves. The traces cut E2M1_K2 on both axes, E4M3_K1 on rows and BF16_K1 on columns. loader_axes is a different claim -- what this build's LOADER does with each shard axis -- and it is checked against tessera.serving.sharding.ROUTE_TP_AXES, which the routes gate on, so the document and the code cannot drift. Since v26 every declared family cuts both axes: a row shard's INITIAL_STATE plane is threaded into the decoder's pad by every shipping body (the window body's window_bits pad for E4M3_K1 and BF16_K1; the span-2 select plane's SELECT_PAD for E2M1_K2, tessera#492), and the native decode of a shard is held to tessera.stock.materialize_stock at load exactly as a whole unit's is. A serve above max_world_size is unattested, which is the same honest status a rung with no lane_eligibility cell has, and not a refusal. Since v39 TESSERA_E2M1_K2's native span-2 route, whose rank-cut admission the v29 materialising route did not have, is also covered at 2 by a route census (experiments/results/glm53_u1_stub_d_tp2_eager_census.json, replayed by tests/test_glm_u1_tp2_census.py): all 21 modules per rank on the native A4 launches, dense modules cut on both axes and each routed stack's intermediate halved to 1024 (its down projection's row extent); it is a route receipt, not a world_size_receipts entry.

fused_module.fields_note: Inside one vLLM-fused module (q/k/v, gate/up), what every role must SHARE and what is free PER MEMBER. vLLM builds one quant method per module, so the family -- and with it the grid, body, scale plane and input width the route decodes to one tile -- is a module fact. The RATE is not: every decoder in this build reads each role from that role's OWN manifest (fp8_route/bf16_route call prepare_window on unit.body_bits/unit.rates/unit.window_bits per role and concatenate; nvfp4_route packs each role's own rate/arity/memory/half scalars and decodes into that role's row slice). This block is checked against tessera.serving.scheme.FUSED_MODULE_FIELDS, the dict the loader itself gates on, exactly as tensor_parallel.units[].loader_axes is checked against sharding.ROUTE_TP_AXES.
fused_module.sidecar_q256_note: How a fused module's rungs are spelled in the checkpoint's scheme. ONE field, one fact: config_groups[..].scheme.q256 is an integer when every role carries the same rung -- the spelling of every checkpoint written before contract v6, unchanged -- or a list of one integer per role, in the scheme's own roles order, when they differ. A plugin build older than v6 refuses the list form on sight ('q256 must be an integer'), which is the fail-closed direction; a v6 build reads both.
fused_module.mixed_rung_receipt_note: Whether a CONTAINER RECEIPT covers a served module whose members took different rungs. It is false: the relaxation is proven by a decode identity (a real Qwen3-0.6B q/k/v at three rungs decodes element-for-element to what the three roles decode alone -- experiments/fused_member_rung_identity.py, tests/test_fused_member_rungs.py), not by a vLLM serve. This is the same distinction loader_axes draws against max_world_size: what the loader accepts is not what a receipt has covered. lane_eligibility is UNCHANGED by this version, so a mixed-rung module's cells resolve exactly as its members' rungs do individually -- unattested where no cell names the rung, which is the honest status and not a refusal.

Publish the default-off decode-once E4M3 dense prefill lane (tessera#931). Under TESSERA_E4M3_DECODE_ONCE=1 the FP8 dense route decodes each RESIDENT module once at load to plain E4M3 bytes, through the module's own Triton window decoder (exact: unit row scale on an FP8 identity), and serves M >= 256 with torch._scaled_mm row-wise on the unchanged E4M3 epilogue contract: same bytes, same per-token activation and per-row weight scales, only the fp32 summation order differs. The lane is EAGER-ONLY: its M branch is host Python, so fp8_route refuses the flag AT LOAD when vLLM's compilation mode is not NONE (PreparedDenseNativeModule.apply also raises under torch.compile, as a backstop only), and a module holding the copy declares a distinct compile-cache dispatch fact (window op|decode-once op). With the flag unset the route never reads the token count to stamp a pair, exactly as at v55. One launch row enters scheme.ROUTE_LAUNCHES[TESSERA_FP8]: (tessera.serving.e4m3_prefill.prefill_apply, native_window_decode_once_e4m3), dense, both regimes, resident only, no extension lane. It enters EXPERIMENTAL_LAUNCHES at the same time, so no cell names it and a v10 lane reader resolves every cell exactly as at v55. The decoded copy (one byte per weight plus the fp32 row scale) is counted in the module's residency accounting (named_tensors). No cell, rung, image, default, artifact or ship gate moves. The pair leaves EXPERIMENTAL_LAUNCHES when a served census of a T-8-projection artifact with the flag on records it. Evidence: docs/measurements/2026-10-04-e4m3-decode-once-prefill.md.

A new top-level block, stock_kernel_overrides (tessera.serving.ext.STOCK_KERNEL_OVERRIDES), publishes where the plugin, behind an opt-in flag, replaces a kernel of the STOCK runtime with its own -- an attention backend's prefill call, a stock unquantized linear. native_extensions publishes the libraries a Tessera ROUTE decodes its wire through; an override reads no Tessera wire, belongs to no route, and claims something else: that it computes the stock kernel's output bit for bit. THE ENTRY (closed, every field validated, contract._validate_stock_kernel_overrides): kind (the kinds this package overrides; attention_backend is the first, and each kind's overrides object has its own closed fields -- attention_backend: backend, the vLLM AttentionBackendEnum member replaced, and kernel, the stock kernel whose call is intercepted); enabled_by (the TESSERA_* flag that installs it, unique); default (off, the only value: an unset flag installs nothing, so a serve that did not ask is the stock serve); loaded_by (the tessera.serving module that installs it); library (the native library it maps, with a native_extensions entry's legibility rules -- module_name_prefix, filename_glob, match basename_fnmatch, a packaged csrc/ source -- or null when it maps none); required_identity (bitwise_vs_stock, the only value); evidence (the gates the identity has passed, {gate, receipt}; [] until one has). AUTHORITY: the block must equal ext.STOCK_KERNEL_OVERRIDES, and an install path acts only when contract.stock_kernel_override_refusal finds its entry under its flag naming exactly the kind, stock object, loader and library it is about to use; otherwise it installs nothing and the refusal is its install line. ONE LIBRARY PER MAPPED NAME across both blocks: no glob in native_extensions or here matches a library name another entry's load path can produce (the native table already held this; it is now checked). THE SCANNER: tests/test_serving_native_extensions.py reads both blocks, so a native load reachable from tessera.serving must match a glob in one of them, and a CDLL, LoadLibrary or load_library call is matched by its path's basename. The block is EMPTY at v54: no override is published, installed or served, and no route, cell, rung, flag, launch, executes list or served byte moves. ADDITIVE for a reader that reads the top level by key (PrismaQuant's); NOT additive for one that refuses unknown top-level keys. A consumer that fingerprints native residency from native_extensions alone will not see an override's library once one is published; it must read this block too.

The value library's dense launch reads column rates 9..14 (Refs #750, item 4 of the T-16 worker): tessera_routed_fused_value's lane.requires.column_rates moves from [1..8] to [1..14]; its column_rates_routed_moe stays [1..8], so a routed stack at 9..14 keeps the compact adapter, and the two E4M3 libraries' lanes do not move. THE KERNEL: csrc/routed_fused_window.cu's RATE_MAX is 14 on the value library and 8 on the E4M3 ones (their grids' codes are 8 bits) and bounds the dense launch only; ROUTED_RATE_MAX (8) bounds both routed launches, and each library publishes both. The dense launch instantiates the one-run rates 9..14 and the pairs 8/9..13/14 at three word stages: the 28-word slot of rates 13 and 14 takes 80,144 B of sm_121's 101,376 B opt-in block. The two-table gate/up launch cannot hold rate 9's 20-word slot even at two stages (101,840 B), and the routed down launch reads the same run tables as its stack's gate/up, so neither is built above 8. decode_rows re-aligns an NZ-word window per lane (three words up to rate 8, four at 9..12, five at 13 and 14). Rates 1..8 keep the three named window words and statements of v49's kernel, so their SASS does not move: a host nvcc build of each library against v49's source gives E4M3 107 of 107 and E4M3-MMA 137 of 137 kernels byte-identical, and value 76 of 77, the dense (7, 8) pair differing by one reassociated shared-memory address with equal instruction and register counts (docs/measurements/2026-09-30-t16-dense-rates-9-14.md). Rates 15 and 16 are excluded by geometry: their 15- and 16-bit windows need 64 KB and 128 KB tables, which leave the one-table block one word stage and none. routed_fused.DENSE_RATE_MAX and dense_rates restate the ceiling and the library is checked against them at load. THE LOADER: compact_prep.prepare_window_compact takes the caller's rate bound; the dense route passes DENSE_WINDOW_RATE_MAX (14) and the routed intake keeps WINDOW_GEMM_RATE_MAX (8). The Triton dense window GEMM already decodes every rate its window holds, so a dense unit at 9..14 whose shape the fused identity refuses keeps the Triton lane. serving_parts.resident_mode_bytes prices a native dense unit up to the same bound. THE RULE (lane schema v11, #750): TESSERA_BF16_K1 publishes allowable_rungs, the second family to do so: window_rate_set, code_arity 1, range_q256 [256, 3584], step_q256 1, run_tables every one-run rate [1]..[14] and every adjacent pair [1,2]..[13,14], excluded_run_tables [] and excluded_q256 [] (the exclusion verdict on two-run tables is pending on #750, as on the E4M3 row), wire the BF16 recipe every attested BF16 rung is stamped with (window, span 1, channel plane, window_bits 14, seed 0, sigma null, channel_sigma 1.0), evidence docs/measurements/2026-09-30-t16-run-tables.md and docs/measurements/2026-09-30-t16-dense-rates-9-14.md. The range stops at 3584 because the wire does: above rate 14 export.wire_recipe widens the window table to the rate (15 and 16 bits), which is a different wire and the geometry that excludes rates 15 and 16. The oracle behind the run tables: tests/test_routed_fused_window.py (both routed launches, rates 1..8 and every pair, v49) and tests/test_dense_fused_window.py (the dense identity, rates 1..14 and every pair: one-hot bitwise decode, the derived bound, graph replay, and random fractional mixes placed at random inside every pair up to 13/14). THE RULE IS FAMILY-WIDE; COVERAGE IS PER CELL. A cell's run tables are derived from its census rungs, and the routed launches read rates 1..8 only, so no routed_moe cell can carry a table above [8]: a rung the rule admits is not servable in every structure, and a consumer asks contract.cell_covers_rung of the cell for its structure. THE CELLS: the eight BF16 cells carry their derived run_tables. The four dense resident cells (decode and batch, and their runtime_1bd4e905 twins) cover [[3,4],[4],[4,5]], so a dense BF16 module is exportable at every rung of 769..1279 (511 rungs) where v50 named their census rungs only. No cell's rungs reach rate 9, so no rung above 8 is covered yet; a dense census at those rates is what covers them. Allowable rungs become a RULE over run tables (lane_eligibility.schema v10 -> v11, tessera#750; Rob 2026-09-30: every valid rate is allowable except ones whose geometry makes them intrinsically worse). A window-grammar rung is a mix of at most two adjacent column rates -- its run table, grammar.rate_set of its per-code root -- and the fused kernels are instantiated per run table, the mix fraction and the upper-rate columns' placement being runtime data; so the kernel oracle attests a VARIANT and every rung of that run table is the same kernel. NEW formats[] FIELD allowable_rungs (optional; on TESSERA_E4M3_K1 only): {rule: window_rate_set, code_arity 1 (the grid's weights per code, validated, so a reader resolves a rung to its run table as rate_set(q256 * code_arity / 256) without knowing the grid), range_q256 [256, 2048], step_q256 1, run_tables [1] [1,2] [2] ... [7,8] [8], excluded_run_tables [], excluded_q256 [], wire (the one wire.recipes entry every allowable rung is cut on), evidence}. A rung q is allowable when it lies in range on step, is not in excluded_q256, and its run table is in run_tables and not in excluded_run_tables (contract.rung_allowable); an unknown rule admits nothing. The run tables are the ones tests/test_routed_fused_window.py and tests/test_dense_fused_window.py attest on GPU: every one-run rate and every adjacent pair, bitwise one-hot decode on both routed launches and the dense identity, within the derived bounds, and graph replay, plus random fractional mixes inside every pair placed at random (docs/measurements/2026-09-30-t8-run-tables.md). NEW CELL FIELD run_tables (v11): the run tables of the cell's census rungs that the family's rule admits, DERIVED by the validator and refused when it differs (contract.derived_cell_run_tables). A cell covers a rung when the rung is a census rung (rungs_q256) or the rule admits it and its run table is one of the cell's (contract.cell_covers_rung, the one predicate scheme.refuse_unserveable_wire, the census join and export_serving's attested_by read). The ten E4M3 cells: dense decode/batch (streamed) [[4]]; dense and routed_moe decode/batch resident, on image f8dbe1a0 and on the v48 nightly image, [[3,4],[4],[4,5]]. So a routed E4M3 stack is exportable at every rung of 769..1279 (511 rungs) where v47 named 8, and dense resident likewise; rungs outside a cell's run tables still need a census. UNCHANGED: attested_rungs_q256, attested_wire and cell rungs_q256 keep listing the census rungs, one stamp per census rung; an attested rung the rule admits must be stamped with the rule's wire (validated). No route, flag, launch, executes list, TP/EP bound or served byte moves. THE KERNEL: the composed decode table is the E4M3 bytes native[codes[state]] (uint8 [E, 2^14], 16 KB per table; routed_fused.compose_table8 / compose_dense_table), the decoded weights go to the B tile as bytes, the per-token e4m3 activation is staged unconverted, and the accumulator is fp32; the B tile is k-major with an XOR swizzle on its 16-byte units and is read by ldmatrix.trans plus a byte permute into the k32 fragment, the A tile is row-major 32 bytes per row with its units staged in fragment order, and the epilogue reads the same accumulator elements in a different register order and applies the same fp32 epilogue (acc * a_scale * w_scale, the SwiGLU, one bf16 rounding). A cell can name the Tessera code its evidence was taken on. Its runtime block accepts two OPTIONAL fields, stamped together or not at all: tessera_commit (the 40-hex commit, for a person to find the tree) and serving_source_sha256 (tessera.serving.source_identity.serving_source_sha256 of that tree, for a program to compare, because an editable install records no commit). The digest covers every source file in the package (each .py file and each native source under tessera/), hashed as paths relative to the directory holding the tessera package, under algorithm tessera.package_source.v1; the whole package rather than a computed serving closure, because a closure can be short and the package cannot. The route trace header carries the same digest of the tree the serve started on, under identity_version 1. No cell carries the fields in this version: none of the fourteen records the tree its evidence was taken on, and a digest is never stamped onto old evidence. Nothing a v40 reader reads changed.

What the fp4 activation quantizer EMITS, read from the kernel (#484). A new top-level activation_quantizers block publishes, per platform and per activation contract, the codes and block-scale bytes the pinned runtime produced for a fixed set of probe inputs. ADDITIVE: no format, cell, rung, route, launch, grade, KL entry, qualification, TP/EP bound or served byte moves, lane_eligibility.schema does not move, and a reader that knows nothing of this key reads the document exactly as it did at v24. WHY A NAME WAS NOT ENOUGH. activation_contract publishes 'e2m1_group16_ue4m3_static', which says the grid, the group and the scale dtype and does not say how a value becomes a code. nvfp4_route.apply hands the artifact's trellis_input_global_scale to vLLM's compiled torch.ops._C.scaled_fp4_quant, so the rounding decision is the runtime's; the document carried no round, rcp, saturate, clamp or amax anywhere, and executes names the launch, not the arithmetic. A consumer pricing the A side therefore had to re-implement the quantizer and call its own model a runtime fact. RobTand/prismaquant#567 is that bill coming due: with the global scale and every group's block scale bit-identical on both sides, the codes disagreed on 3.43% of elements, each by exactly one E2M1 step. WHAT IT PUBLISHES. Eleven probe groups at the points where two honest implementations of this contract diverge: the seven E2M1 midpoints at four used scales (1.0, 1.5 at two global scales, and 1.75 -- three of the four have inexact F32 reciprocals), those midpoints one BF16 ulp either side, every E2M1 code with both signs and both zeros, element saturation above the top code, the UE4M3 block-scale underflow tie at amax = 6*2**-10, the value one BF16 ulp above it, and the block-scale overflow past 448. The inputs are the repository's (serving/activation_attestation.py constructs them in BF16 bit patterns and the validator refuses an edited one); the outputs came from the operator and from nowhere else, generated by experiments/attest_activation_quantizer.py, which the block names so a reader knows what to re-run. WHAT THE RUNTIME ANSWERED, on sm_121 in the image versions.default_serve_image pins, vLLM 0.28.0 / torch 2.13.0+cu130 on a GB10 at driver 595.84: round-to-nearest with ties to the EVEN ENCODED INDEX, identical at all four used scales -- 0.25->0, 0.75->1.0, 1.25->1.0, 1.75->2.0, 2.5->2.0, 3.5->4.0, 5.0->4.0. One BF16 ulp off a midpoint resolves to the exact-nearest code every time, at every scale, so the element path carries no intermediate coarser than that. The block scale ties to zero at 2**-10 (byte 0x00, whole group zero) and SATURATES to 448 (byte 0x7e) at 512 rather than emitting E4M3 NaN. This is a negative result for the leading hypothesis about prismaquant#567 and it is published as one: on every boundary this table reaches, the kernel does what PrismaQuant's oracle models, so the 3.43% divergence is not a tie-break, not a saturation convention and not a coarse element intermediate. WHAT IT DOES NOT REACH. Every probe is exact on both sides by construction -- a table whose inputs are inexact could not be checked without the checker owning the runtime's own arithmetic, which is the thing being avoided. So this attests behaviour at exactly representable global and block scales and says nothing about a non-dyadic used scale, which is what a served artifact actually carries. Closing that needs a bulk differential measurement, not a contract table. VALIDATION. validate_serving_contract now requires the block and validates it against the CELLS: an attestation for a platform lane_eligibility does not publish, or for a contract nothing on that platform executes, is refused. Absence is not a default -- a platform or a contract with no entry publishes no attestation at all, and a consumer gate must refuse the route rather than fall back to its own model. Only sm_121 and only e2m1_group16_ue4m3_static are attested here; fp8_per_token_dynamic, bf16_unquantized and the two AMD platforms are additive under the same schema and are not filled in to look complete. Every check the validator makes is 'a nearest encoding, or one of two tied nearest' and never 'this encoding', because which side of a tie the kernel takes is the fact being published.

One cell per regime rather than one per (regime, residency), which is the sm_121 dense BF16 precedent: per-residency KL was measured here in both regimes and came back bit-identical, so the residency is not an axis these receipts distinguish, and a four-cell split would publish a distinction the measurement refuses. EVIDENCE. grade kl_lower_bound on both, each from a top-1024 teacher-student intersection bound scored in the CELL'S OWN regime against the unquantized model served on the same image: KL >= 0.004906 over 4088 prefill-scored positions for batch, KL >= 0.004804 over 256 M=1 positions for decode. A full-vocabulary KL is NOT claimed, and the reason is measured rather than conceded: no instrument in this repository produces one (docs/measurements/moe-evidence-debt-2026-09-04.md section 4). qualification device_qualified, and the receipt carries the scope line it is qualified under: gfx1201 under WSL2 proves the HIP code path; it says nothing about gfx1151 numerics and nothing about performance on any part. No gfx1151 cell: nobody here owns that hardware, and docs/strix-halo-tester-protocol.md is still what a Strix Halo receipt must satisfy. No routed-MoE cell on gfx1201: the BF16 MoE builder path was not exercised on HIP in this work, so there is no receipt to mint one from. THE RUNTIME IS A SECOND IMAGE ON A SECOND BACKEND. runtime.image is a private-registry digest reference, port-less, which is what runtime_image._DIGEST_REFERENCE accepts (a repository component may not carry a colon, so host:5000/... is unpinnable by this grammar); docker's own RepoDigests for the pulled image carries the port-less spelling, so the pin is the daemon's answer and not a re-spelling of it. runtime.vllm and runtime.torch are transcribed from the in-container banner of the serves the receipts were taken through. versions.default_serve_image does not move: it is still the sm_121 dense image, and v10 only requires it to equal SOME platform's serve_image. Lane-eligibility schema v10 (#456): the table gains a PLATFORM AXIS, so the document can say what a platform executes before any cell on it exists. WHAT WAS MISSING: platforms was a set of KEYS -- the only thing read of it was whether a cell's platform was declared -- and a cell is a RECEIPT, so the only way to say anything about a platform was to have served on it. There is no way in v9 to publish the fact that a family has no native route on a device, which is precisely what an RDNA3.5 or RDNA4 box needs said about E2M1 and E4M3 before a model load reaches a kernel. Silence had to stand in for it, and silence is not an attestation. WHAT THE FIELD IS: every platforms[key] now carries backend (cuda | hip), exactly one of compute_capability / gcn_arch, a serve_image that is a digest iff the platform has at least one cell and null otherwise, and executes -- a map over every family in formats[] whose value is that family's OWN route contract or null. Non-null is checked against scheme.ROUTES, never transcribed: a platform cannot claim a contract the dispatch does not run. null means unbacked, and it is a claim somebody looked. A platform key the table does not carry means nothing at all, which is a third state and not a synonym for null -- the plugin reads the three as backed / unbacked / unstated (contract.platform_execution_contract, #455) and refuses only on unbacked. WHAT SHIPS: sm_121 gains backend, serve_image and executes with its three existing contracts; gfx1151 and gfx1201 arrive as entries with serve_image null, no cells, BF16 backed and E4M3/E2M1 null. Tessera-16 (TESSERA_BF16_K1, W16A16) is the AMD lane; the quantized families are unbacked there because the pinned runtime has no native route for those bytes on those devices, not because a kernel is unwritten. gfx1150 is compiled for and gets no entry until someone intends to serve on it. NO AMD CELL: a cell is a device receipt and none has been taken, so v23 publishes none. The gfx1151 entry exists with no cell precisely because nobody here owns the hardware; what a Strix Halo receipt must contain and the scope line it carries are in docs/strix-halo-tester-protocol.md (#459), and a receipt arriving turns that entry into cells at v24 without editing the entry. THREE RULES ADDED. A cell on a null executes entry is refused -- an unbacked platform states the fact in executes, it does not mint cells. qualification compile_only is incompatible with route_status backed or backed_with_serve_flag: a compile receipt proves a toolchain fact and a backed claim needs a device. This moves no existing cell (v22 carries zero compile_only cells; all ten are backed_with_serve_flag and device_qualified), and the ten sm_121 cells are byte-identical under v23 -- tests/fixtures/lane_eligibility_cells_v22.json records that array's SHA-256, byte length and cell count and tests/test_contract_platform_axis.py hashes the same span of this file. A digest rather than a copy on purpose: the array holds the runtime image pin and tests/test_runtime_image_pin.py refuses a second copy of that digest in any file that acts, so a hash pins the same bytes without holding the pin. And a platform's serve_image must be an image at least one of its OWN cells attests, with versions.default_serve_image equal to some platform's serve_image. THAT LAST RULE IS WEAKER THAN THE DESIGN ASKED FOR, DELIBERATELY: the design said every cell's runtime.image equals its platform's serve_image, and the shipped document falsifies it -- sm_121 already carries TWO attested images, the eight dense cells on the vanilla pin and the two routed_moe cells on a second build. Taken literally the rule would refuse the contract that is in this file. Measured, not softened: the per-structure statement is what test_the_default_serve_image_is_the_dense_cells_image now says, per platform. NOT ADDITIVE, and the schema string says so: a v9 reader must not read a v10 document, because a platform entry is now an object with meaning rather than a key, and a reader that went on treating platforms as a key set would read an unbacked platform as an ordinary one. A closed reader refuses v10 by name, which is the designed fail-closed and the whole reason the schema is versioned. No rung, route, activation contract, launch, grade, KL entry, qualification, TP/EP bound or served byte moved.

Lane-eligibility schema v9 (#327): a smoke's status word is DERIVED from a machine-readable record and checked, and the residual observation the record holds is readable by a consumer again. WHAT WAS WRONG: the per-completion rule was stated and pinned, but the AGGREGATION from a set of completions to the cell's ONE published word was stated exactly once, in a dated measurement file, in the existential form 'at least one prompt reads recorded on both arms in the campaign form'. Nothing in the repository said why 'some' rather than 'all'; nothing derived it; no test computed it (tests/test_cell_evidence.py verified the word by substring-matching two markdown lines of the receipt, so re-running the smoke with a different result changed no test); and the condition was satisfiable by an EMPTY completion, because classify([]) returned recorded. A rule that decides a field a serving gate reads does not live in append-only history, and a gate that cannot catch its own defect is not a gate (AGENTS.md 2, 4, 10). The existential's own justification did not fit the rows that satisfied it either: 'campaign' labels a SAMPLING SHAPE, and the three prompts carrying the positive record are chat turns through the checkpoint's own template, an INTERFACE the v17 campaign never sent. Worse, v21 retired smoke.control in the same release, so after it no cell carried a control, all ten read unattributed, and a consumer at the pin could not tell the two routed_moe cells -- whose smoke cycles on seven of fourteen completions -- from the two dense BF16 cells whose smoke never cycled at all. WHAT THE FIELD IS: smoke gains record, either null or the closed {instrument, rule, reference, rows}. instrument is the repository path to the code that owns the per-completion rule; rule is that code's own statement of it, quoted verbatim, so the rule is readable at the pin (the wheel does not ship experiments/, and a tree test pins the two equal); reference is null or a name from contract.EVIDENCE_CONTROL_REFERENCES; rows is a non-empty set of distinct (prompt, form) pairs, each {prompt, form, interface, status, reference_status} with the verdicts from EVIDENCE_SMOKE_STATUSES, interface from EVIDENCE_SMOKE_INTERFACES (raw_completion | chat_template) and form from EVIDENCE_SMOKE_FORMS (campaign | pure_greedy). No number lives in a cell here either: L, the period and the periodic suffix stay in the receipt and the record carries the verdicts read off them. THE AGGREGATION, in one home (contract.derive_smoke_status, restated in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md beside the grade and attribution derivations and nowhere else): repetitive when some row cycles on this arm and the reference does not -- a degeneration the reference does not share is this route's, and that is the whole content of the word; else recorded when some row reads recorded on this arm AND on the reference (on this arm alone when no reference was run), which is the positive record principle 5's 'generates correctly' leg asks for; else repetitive when any row cycles at all; else not_recorded. The threshold is neither 'some prompt' nor 'all prompts': it is derived from what the word is a claim ABOUT. status is a claim about this ROUTE, so an observation the unquantised reference reproduces is not this route's -- the same principle schema v7's control was added for, applied per (prompt, form) instead of once per cell. attribution is now derived from the record when there is one and from the v7 control when there is not, and a smoke carrying BOTH is refused by name: one derivation, one home. WHAT MOVED ON THE TABLE: no status word moved. Both routed_moe cells still publish recorded, and it is now the word their own record derives -- 14 rows, 6 reading recorded on both arms, 7 cycling on the student, all 7 of those cycling on the BF16 source too, 0 cycling on the student while the source answered. What moved is attribution on those two cells, unattributed -> shared_with_reference, DERIVED and checked: that is the field that makes the residual repetitive observation machine-readable, and it is what now separates these cells from the two dense BF16 cells (recorded, unattributed, no reference arm). The consumer rule ARCHITECTURE.md documents -- refuse on status 'repetitive' AND attribution other than 'shared_with_reference', never on status alone -- has a real cell to read again. THE INTERFACE FINDING, CARRIED: every row names the interface it was taken on, so a consumer reads what the measurement actually found -- through the checkpoint's own chat_template.jinja both arms answer with their own EOS; under raw continuation both arms, student AND BF16 source, end in a cycle. That could not be carried at v8: v8's smoke has one slot for a word that is interface-dependent, and v8's control.outcome vocabulary (identical_completion | different_completion) was written for a ONE-prompt smoke -- on a 14-completion record a bare identical_completion cannot say WHICH prompt, which would be true about the observation and misleading about its meaning, the exact defect v18 was invented to stop. AN ASSERTED STATUS, NAMED: record is nullable, and a cell whose record is null publishes an ASSERTED status -- a word a person read off a receipt, which nothing here can check and which contract.smoke_status_is_derived reports False for. The two dense BF16 cells are in that state: their receipt records one greedy continuation from four census arms of the same route, with no per-completion scoring and no reference arm, so there is no per-(prompt, form) table to transcribe and nothing here invents one. What would give them a derived status is a measurement and not an edit -- experiments/moe_greedy_smoke.py run against a serve of that artifact with its own tokenizer and a BF16 reference arm beside it. The six not_recorded cells never ran a smoke. THE EMPTY-COMPLETION HOLE, CLOSED WHERE THE CONDITION IS DECIDED: classify([]) is not_recorded, so two arms that both return '' for one prompt can no longer manufacture a positive record out of two non-answers; the instrument's RULE string gains the clause. Every completion the 2026-09-05 receipt scored is non-empty (L is 16, 64 or 292-512 on all fourteen rows), so no verdict in it moves. NOT ADDITIVE, and the schema string says so: a v8 reader must not read a v9 document, because record is a key its closed smoke object does not know and because -- the reason the version exists -- a v8 reader goes on treating a status word as asserted prose when it is now the checked output of a stated rule. No rung, route, activation contract, launch, grade, KL entry, qualification, TP/EP bound or byte moved; the decode cell still grades route_only and the evidence debt of docs/measurements/moe-evidence-debt-2026-09-04.md is unchanged. NOT a claim the route is fault-free: a smoke is one prompt family under one runtime, the record now says on which interfaces it cycled, and the receipt says the rest.

Both routed_moe cells' evidence.smoke read 'recorded' (#198), on a Tessera measurement: docs/measurements/moe-smoke-recorded-2026-09-05.md. WHAT WAS WRONG: the cells published smoke.status 'repetitive' with a control saying the BF16 source returns the same ' France is France is ...' (v18), and a status-only consumer kept refusing the whole routed-MoE lane -- rightly under its rule, because a control that degenerates too removes the evidence AGAINST the route without adding any FOR it. Principle 5's 'generates correctly' leg had no positive record for routed MoE; the honest fix is a positive record, which is a measurement and not a predicate change on either side. WHAT WAS MEASURED: the E4M3/q1024 LFM2.5-8B-A1B student (seal-bound, read-only) and its BF16 source, one arm at a time on the same pinned image, eager, resident, TP=1, no speculative decoding, the checkpoint's generation_config defaults in force; seven prompts in two request forms (the campaign's shape; pure greedy), every completion kept verbatim on both arms. Raw continuation -- the v17 prompt and three passages ending mid-sentence -- ends in a cycle on the SOURCE on all eight (prompt, form) pairs and on the student on seven: the checkpoint is the instruct model and a raw continuation is not its trained interface. Through the checkpoint's own chat_template.jinja (byte-identical on both arms) three questions carrying the same content read 'recorded' on BOTH arms in BOTH forms: no cycle, an on-topic answer, the model's own EOS on all six student completions. The rule: repetitive iff the completion ends in a cycle (some period p with 2p <= L has a p-periodic suffix holding >= 2 full periods) on the student tokenizer's canonical encoding; the v17 observation is its positive control and reads repetitive on both arms in the same receipt. The completions are not identical between arms and nothing is claimed about that: this is greedy coherence, not closeness; the batch cell's KL entry is the closeness record and does not move. WHAT MOVED ON THE TABLE: both routed_moe cells' smoke is {status recorded, receipt the file above, attribution unattributed, control null} -- the shape the two BF16 cells already record theirs in. The v18 control is retired from the cells and not from the record: the v8 control vocabulary attributes a SYMPTOM ('identical_completion' says the reference returned the same text, 'different_completion' that it did not), and a recorded smoke has none to attribute -- the arms' recorded completions differ, so 'identical_completion' would be false of them and 'different_completion' would derive not_shared_with_reference, a phrase written for a symptom the reference lacks, said of a healthy pair. Null is what is true; attribution is what the validator derives for it, not hand-written. What the control established stands and is re-measured in the receipt (the v17 prompt identical on both arms, character for character). A schema that could say 'reference arm run, both healthy' would be v9 and no consumer has asked for it. No rung, route, activation contract, launch, grade, KL entry, qualification, TP/EP bound or byte moved; the decode cell still grades route_only and the evidence debt of docs/measurements/moe-evidence-debt-2026-09-04.md is one leg shorter, not closed. ADDITIVE for readers: lane-eligibility schema stays v8 (no field changed shape); a v8 consumer that refused on status 'repetitive' now admits on status 'recorded' with no change of its own, which is the point. NOT a claim the route is fault-free: a smoke is one prompt family under one runtime, and the receipt says so.

native_extensions[tessera_window_gemv].lane.requires publishes the lane's WHOLE predicate (#264): release_overrides false, diagonals false, rotation ['none'], start_state false and grid_arities [1] join the four conditions of v12. WHAT WAS WRONG: the loader (kernel_window_gemv.prepare_from_parsed) refuses nine conditions by name on the same bytes, and the five above were published nowhere, so the two gates that decide 'can this lane read this wire' from this block -- scheme.refuse_unreachable_lane at plan time and scheme.lane_wire_report at byte time (tools/tessera_lane_preflight.py) -- declared READABLE, exit 0, wire the loader refuses module by module. The live case is a TP row shard: layout.slice_unit stamps an INITIAL_STATE plane the kernel cannot take (serving/csrc/window_gemv.cu supplies state_{-1} = 0 itself; the L-bit pad that opens a wire column is not stored), the preflight said READABLE, and every module fell back at load -- #104/#206 one condition class over. WHAT THE FIELDS ARE: release_overrides, diagonals and start_state are booleans -- whether the lane reads a unit that CARRIES the thing (false: it does not; the kernel decodes straight off the wire, applies no diagonals, takes no start state); rotation is the list of rotation states the lane reads, in the checkpoint dialect ('none', 'r_in_only') the body and plane fields already speak; grid_arities is the list of grid arities (the kernel decodes one code per position). DELIBERATELY NOT PUBLISHED: prepare_from_parsed's scalar-256-native grid clause. That is an entry-point fact of the E4M3 table build, not a lane fact: the same extension reads BF16 window wire through prepare_value_unit, whose scalar grid has 65536 codes, so publishing size/native would declare wire unreadable that the lane serves -- a false claim in the refusing direction -- while every unit the published predicate admits on the FP8 route carries the scalar-256 native grid by construction (that is what the E4M3 grid is). ONE HOME: the decision is scheme.decide_lane_requirements, which the byte-time report, the plan-time gate, the loader itself and bf16_route.gemv_refusal_for_unit all run over this block (the validator pins the block to ext.NATIVE_EXTENSIONS exactly as before), so predicate == loader by construction rather than by three restatements that drift. PLAN DECIDABILITY, correcting v12's premise that every requires field is a function of (grid, q256): rotation, diagonals and releases are statements a plan makes and refuse_unreachable_lane now takes them (defaults are the exporter's own pinned plan -- whole, undecorated units on a scalar grid); start_state is a property of a LATER slice, so the plan gate decides the plan's own statement while the byte-time gate reads it off the wire, which is where the shard case is caught. The plan gate also now REFUSES a published requirement it has not learned instead of skipping it -- the plan-time twin of the #206 rule the byte-time reader already had. NOT ADDITIVE: a v19 validator refuses these fields (closed LANE_REQUIREMENT_FIELDS), which is the fail-closed direction, and a byte-time reader that has not learned a class refuses every unit rather than passing the subset it knows (lane_wire_report raises on an unknown requirement, #206). The preflight report schema stays tessera.lane_preflight/2: its shape -- the requirements and refusals beside every verdict -- is unchanged; only the requirement roster it relays grows. No rung, route, range, cell, launch, activation contract, TP/EP bound or wire byte moves; column_rates and window_bits are still the parse of csrc/window_gemv.cu.

Lane-eligibility schema v8 (#198), pre-release evidence correction: evidence.artifact is required and is null when no encoder-reproduction comparison is recorded. Otherwise it names the historical artifact and full encoder commit, plus the exact re-encode commit, single unit, payload relation, weight_sse relation and receipt. The four dense E4M3 cells name the checkpoint built at 8070ec6; a same-source down_proj comparison at 3317036 (also measured before wire minor 7 at 1e58fdc) finds a different payload and slightly lower weight SSE. Lane-eligibility schema v7 (#195): a greedy smoke names the CONTROL it was compared against, so a consumer can tell "this route degenerates" from "this prompt degenerates on this model". WHAT WAS WRONG: both routed_moe cells published smoke.status 'repetitive', an accurate record of what came back, and a producer-side gate refused the whole routed-MoE lane on it -- correctly under the rule it was given, because principle 9 requires a route to generate correctly. Then the control was run: the same prompt, byte for byte from experiments/tessera_plugin_served.sh, against the BF16 SOURCE on the same pinned image, eager, returns ' France is France is ...' character for character identical to the Tessera student's (docs/measurements/moe-evidence-debt-2026-09-04.md section 7). The repetition is the model and the prompt, not the quantisation -- and that fact lived in prose while the field a gate reads said 'repetitive'. A machine-readable value true about the observation and misleading about its meaning, with the disambiguating measurement unreadable by any consumer, is principle 14 one level up, which is why the fix is in the schema and not in either consumer. WHAT THE FIELD IS: smoke gains control, either null or the closed {reference, outcome, receipt} -- reference from contract.EVIDENCE_CONTROL_REFERENCES ('bf16_source', the unquantised source the route is a quantisation of), outcome from EVIDENCE_CONTROL_OUTCOMES, receipt a repository path under docs/measurements/ like every other receipt here (grammar in the validator, existence in a tree test). WHAT OUTCOME ESTABLISHES, EXACTLY: 'identical_completion' means the reference returned the SAME completion for the same prompt under the smoke's own runtime and execution mode; 'different_completion' means the completions differ -- NOT that the reference was healthy, which no string comparison can decide. WHAT A CONSUMER READS: attribution, DERIVED from control and checked, exactly as grade is derived from kl -- no control 'unattributed' (nobody ran the reference, so the status is an observation and not an attribution), 'identical_completion' 'shared_with_reference', 'different_completion' 'not_shared_with_reference' (weaker than 'the route is at fault', and deliberately not spelled that way). A gate that refused on status alone now refuses on status 'repetitive' AND attribution other than 'shared_with_reference', which is the pair that carries the decision. NO scope FIELD: a smoke record carries no scope of its own, a control cannot be better scoped than the thing it controls, and that the arms match is what the receipt attests -- as for every other receipt-backed field here. ONE control and not a list, deliberately: one is what has been run, and a second reference is a bump rather than a surprise. WHAT MOVED ON THE TABLE: the two routed_moe cells carry the control above and read shared_with_reference; the eight dense cells carry control null and attribution 'unattributed' -- six of them never ran a smoke and the two BF16 cells ran one with no reference arm. No status word changed: 'repetitive' is still what came back. No rung, route, activation contract, launch, grade, KL entry, qualification, TP/EP bound or byte moved. NOT ADDITIVE, and the schema string says so: a v6 reader must not read a v7 document, both because attribution and control are keys its closed smoke object does not know and because -- the reason the version exists -- a v6 reader goes on making a decision off status that status no longer carries alone. The same release also corrected the three build-box absolute paths in this changelog's own prose (#181, contract v17, prose-only and unversioned); this entry is the schema half.

Lane-eligibility schema v6 (#131, #133): a cell names its own evidence instead of borrowing a global. (1) versions.attested_on is REMOVED. It did double duty -- the toolchain the contract was written against and the runtime the cells were measured on -- and was false for the two routed_moe cells, which were measured on eugr/spark-vllm@sha256:0afec8d4... under vLLM 0.28.1rc1.dev397+gfd4a15126.d20260904, not vllm/vllm-openai under 0.28.0. Each cell's runtime now carries the vllm and torch build its OWN receipt records (dense: 0.28.0 / 2.13.0+cu130 per tessera-window-gemv-served-2026-09-03.md and tessera-bf16-route-served-2026-09-02.md; routed_moe: the census receipt docs/measurements/census/lfm25-8b-a1b-served-r4.json versions block), beside the v5 image and execution_modes scope; the validator requires all four and refuses two toolchains under one digest. versions is now closed to {tessera, plugin_entry_point, default_serve_image} and every field is checked: tessera non-empty, plugin_entry_point the one this package registers, default_serve_image an exact digest that some cell attests. default_serve_image is the serve-image pin harnesses read (runtime_image.PIN_CONTRACT_FIELD, previously versions.attested_on.image); its value is the dense cells' image and did not move. The old device field is dropped: platform and compute_capability already carry it. (2) Every cell carries a required, closed evidence object {grade, kl[], smoke} so a gate can read what grade of evidence the cell rests on, never prose. PREMISE CORRECTION recorded here because it decides the values: every served KL this repository holds, dense and MoE alike, is a kl_tool top-1024 teacher/student-intersection LOWER BOUND, so no cell grades kl_full_vocab and 'the MoE cells carry screen-grade evidence while the dense cells do not' is not the distinction. The distinctions are which REGIME the bound was scored in, under which execution modes, whether a greedy smoke is on record, and the population (one Qwen3-0.6B artifact per dense family; one LFM2.5-8B-A1B artifact for routed_moe). A kl entry is {kind, top_k, regime, execution_modes, receipt}; regime must be the cell's own (a prefill bound written into a decode cell is refused), execution_modes a subset of the cell's, receipt a repository path under docs/measurements/ (existence is a tree test). smoke is {status in recorded|repetitive|not_recorded, receipt}. grade is DERIVED from the entries (route_only when no bound in the cell's regime; kl_lower_bound; kl_full_vocab) and checked, like executes. Resulting grades: batch cells all kl_lower_bound (E2M1 and E4M3-resident from tessera-serving-plugin-2026-09-02.md eager+compiled; E4M3-streamed from tessera-window-gemv-served-2026-09-03.md arm A eager+compiled; BF16 from its receipt, eager; routed_moe from tessera-lfm-campaign-2026-09-04.md section 8, eager). Decode cells: only tessera_e4m3_k1_dense_sm121_decode_streamed has a decode-regime bound (tessera-decode-regime-kl-2026-09-03.md eager arm A; tessera-compiled-decode-kl-r6-2026-09-04.md compiled A1/A2); every other decode cell, dense and MoE, is route_only -- the census attests dispatch and nothing attests decode-regime quality. Smoke: BF16 cells recorded (identical greedy continuation, ungraded), routed_moe cells repetitive, all others not_recorded. NOT additive: a v5 reader must not read a v6 document (new required cell keys, versions renamed). No rung, route, activation contract, launch, TP/EP bound or byte moved; the eight dense cells and two routed_moe cells keep their ids and scopes. qualification is unchanged and deliberately not overloaded with the grade; whether route_only routed_moe cells should remain device_qualified is #133's open decision.

native_extensions[tessera_window_gemv].routes gains TESSERA_BF16. The window GEMV is loaded by BOTH window routes -- bf16_route.prepare_bf16_gemv repacks through kernel_window_gemv.prepare_value_unit exactly as fp8_gemv does, sets the same layer.tessera_gemv, and bf16_route.apply branches on it -- and the table said TESSERA_FP8 alone. That is a claim about this runtime narrower than the runtime: a consumer keying reproducibility on native-extension residency (PrismaQuant's serve fingerprint, which is why this block exists) would have read a BF16 serve with the extension and one without as the same serve, and they execute different launches. Found by the tie tests added with lane_eligibility v4: scheme.ROUTE_LAUNCHES gives the 16-bit route the same three launches the 8-bit one has, and test_the_launch_tables_lane_is_the_published_extension asserts every launch's lane names an extension that lists that route. The correction is also load-bearing for v4's own derivation: contract._lanes_a_rung_reaches filters candidate lanes by route, so with the narrower list a TESSERA_BF16_K1 cell could never derive a GEMV launch -- correct today only because the attested rung 1792 is root 7 and unreachable anyway, and silently wrong the day a reachable BF16 rung is attested. NO CELL MOVES: at 1792 the derivation still returns torch.mm over torch_window, because the rung, not the route list, is what refuses the lane there. loaded_by stays tessera.serving.fp8_gemv: the field is a single string by schema and both reaching modules are under tessera.serving, so it still says what it is for -- that this entry is serving-side and not producer-side -- while naming one of the two. lane_eligibility schema v4: every cell publishes `executes`, the (symbol, decoder) launches the route MAKES in that cell's regime at that cell's residency on that cell's rungs -- and the E4M3 family's cells split along the residency, because that is the axis those launches differ on. WHAT WAS WRONG: a cell said which A-side contract ran (correct, and still does: the FP8 route's per-token quantiser runs on every path and hands the GEMV dequantised values, so fp8_per_token_dynamic is what executes in both regimes) and which rungs a receipt covered, and the only place the LAUNCH appeared was the cell's id -- `..._decode_scaled_mm_w8a8`, a string no gate parses. That was accidentally true while the window-GEMV lane was unreachable: every allocated checkpoint carried a rate outside kernel_window_gemv.SUPPORTED_RATES, so an E4M3 decode really did execute the materialised FP8 pair (issue #104). It stopped being true on a rate-constrained Qwen3-0.6B build, uniform q256 1024 (root rate 4 exactly), whose served census records decode: symbol tessera_window_gemv::gemv, decoder window_gemv, 112 of 112 modules; prefill: symbol torch._scaled_mm, decoder window_gemv, 112 of 112 (streamed, eager; receipt docs/measurements/tessera-gemv-lane-reachable-2026-09-03.md, which carries both census rows in section (b) and the experiments/ts104_gemv_census.sh command that produced them -- the census JSON itself is a build-box run log, not a file this distribution carries). A gate reading the contract to decide what the decode regime runs would have read a false value: principle 14 from the other direction, an attested claim gone stale under a checkpoint the runtime can finally serve (issue #111). WHICH REGIME THE TABLE SPEAKS: this contract's, not the kernel's. `decode` here is the ONE-ROW forward and `batch` is every M > 1 (contract.CENSUS_PHASE_REGIMES, which says so in its own words); the kernel's `decode` is M <= GEMV_MAX_M and spans eight token counts. The first cut of this entry read the second into the first and published the batch cell WITHOUT the GEMV -- true of the 64-row prefill the census drives, false of the 2-to-8-row forwards the same regime covers, on which the lane serves its own gemv exactly as it does at one row. So tessera_e4m3_k1_dense_sm121_batch_streamed executes BOTH launches, while the decode cell executes the gemv alone, because decode_is_gemv is unconditionally true at one row (the rate-1 refusal starts at the 4-row tile) -- there is no rate condition on a cell anywhere. tests/test_serving_contract.py::test_the_launch_tables_regimes_are_the_routes_own_dispatch derives both regimes from the routes' own decode_is_gemv over every M the dispatch distinguishes, which is what makes this a derivation and not a second guess. WHAT THE VALUE IS DERIVED FROM: tessera.serving.scheme.ROUTE_LAUNCHES, the torch-free table the routes' OWN fp8_gemv.census_expected / bf16_route.census_expected are built from and which owns WINDOW_GEMV_SYMBOL, narrowed by the three axes a cell already carries -- the regime, the residency its TESSERA_SERVE_MODE flag names (both window routes set layer.tessera_gemv = None in resident, so the lane exists in streamed alone), and the lanes each rung REACHES under the predicate native_extensions[].lane.requires publishes (contract v12), which is kernel_window_gemv's own constants. So a cell naming the GEMV cannot outlive the kernel's rate set: change SUPPORTED_RATES and this document stops validating. WHY THE RESIDENCY SPLIT AND NOT A PREDICATE: the two shapes issue #111 offered were a lane predicate on the cell and an explicit rung condition. The rung condition is kept -- rungs_q256 is an enumerated list and a reader resolves no predicate -- but the rung alone cannot separate the two launches, because the one attested E4M3 rung (1024) is lane-readable and the launch there is decided by the residency, which was already a machine-readable cell field spelled as an OR. Two cells of one (platform, family, structure, regime) must now cover DISJOINT residencies, so a reader's answer cannot depend on the order the cells were written in. Cell IDs no longer name a launch: an id is its scope (family, structure, platform, regime, plus the residency where a cell covers only some), because an id that names a launch is a second unparsed spelling of `executes` -- the one that went stale. NOT ADDITIVE, and the schema string says so: a v3 reader must not read a v4 cell, both because `executes` is a key it does not know and because the E4M3 decode answer it would have taken from one cell is now two. TESSERA_BF16_K1 gains `executes` and NO GEMV cell: its attested rung 1792 is root 7, outside SUPPORTED_RATES, so its own streamed GEMV lane is unreachable and the launch a receipt could cover there is the torch window decode under torch.mm -- which is what the derivation returns, unforced. The day a reachable BF16 rung is attested, the same derivation produces its GEMV cell.

MERGE RENUMBER: this landed on a branch that bumped to 11 while another branch bumped to 11 for `construction`; both merged, so one version number named two contracts and this is the later one. native_extensions[].lane: the decoder this extension's OWN lane stamps on a route record (telemetry's 'decoder' field), and -- where the lane has one -- the wire predicate a unit must satisfy before the lane can read it at all. tessera_window_gemv publishes requires.column_rates [1, 2, 4] and requires.window_bits [14], which ARE kernel_window_gemv.SUPPORTED_RATES and WINDOW_BITS_SUPPORTED (tests/test_lane_reachability.py ties the two ends, the way loader_axes is tied to sharding.ROUTE_TP_AXES): that kernel repacks each column's code stream at that column's own rate and has a 16-row lane only where R bits per code is a whole number of bytes, so R = 3 would need 6-byte lanes and is refused. WHY A PRODUCER NEEDS IT: a rung is a ROOT rate and grammar.bresenham_rate_schedule mixes the two rates bracketing it, so q256 1006 (root 3.93) is columns at rate 3 and columns at rate 4, and EVERY unit of such a checkpoint refuses this lane at load -- silently, module by module, through a substitution the route reports as a served module. All six allocated checkpoints held when this was written carried a rate outside the set (docs/measurements/tessera-gemv-lane-reachable-2026-09-03.md section (a), 'The six allocated checkpoints, read from their bytes', names each one and its rate set off the bytes themselves; the checkpoints are build-box artifacts, not files this distribution carries), so no artifact we held could exercise the lane at all, and four censuses that were meant to measure it recorded 112 of 112 modules on torch_window with an empty problem list (issue #104). With the predicate published, a producer refuses the PLAN -- scheme.refuse_unreachable_lane, called at argument time by experiments/export_tessera_serving.py --require-lane, before one unit is encoded -- and a census counts engagement against lane.decoder instead of reading agreement off a fallback it could not see. The NVFP4 entry publishes lane.decoder native_span2 and NO requires block: its eligibility is the route's own, already in formats[], and an empty block would be a claim of no constraint rather than an absence of one (the validator refuses an empty requires for exactly that reason). ADDITIVE in denotation -- no rung, route, range or activation contract moved, and the lane block only states what the kernel already enforced; it is a version bump and not a silent addition because a validating reader refuses a document without lane, which is what contract_version 11 says.

On Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration that is EVERY attention projection (MLA at models/glm5next/nvidia/model.py:331, the whole KDA layer at kda.py:171-174, the indexer's wk_weights_proj at attention.py:263) and the whole vision tower (model.py:1082): 20 of 24 Linear patterns, 4 offered. ADDITIVE for a reader that reads keys by name; a version bump for a reader that validates, because a document without the block is refused, exactly as v7 did for native_extensions. (Landed as v11: #100 took v10 for the serve-image digest pin while this was in flight.)

ADDITIVE for a reader that reads keys by name: the key and its type are unchanged.

native_extensions: the streamed FP8 route's decode-regime GEMV joins the table. The fused window-body GEMV (tessera_window_gemv, built from csrc/window_gemv.cu through tessera.kernel_window_gemv and reached from tessera.serving.fp8_gemv) reads the E4M3 window wire directly at M <= 8, so the library can be resident in a serving process and the import-graph walk refuses a table without it. Both residencies substitute the torch window decode without it: streamed serves the same verified bytes through decode + _scaled_mm (slower), and resident never needed it (it decodes once at load through the same torch decoder). A GEMV serve stamps decoder window_gemv on its route record, so the fallback stays visible in a census histogram. ADDITIVE for a reader that reads keys by name: every key a v8 reader read is byte-identical. It is a version bump, not a silent addition, for a reader that validates: a document without the entry is refused, which is what contract_version 9 says -- exactly as v7 did for the block itself.

attested_wire: the wire each attested rung was cut on, beside the rung (#55). attested_rungs_q256 says a receipt covered rung 1792; two encoders can write two byte strings at one rung -- the window table the decoder reads lives on the ALPHABET plane, so anything that moves the table moves the bytes while the rung, the route and the decoder stand still -- and until now the table said nothing about which bytes at 1792 (it mentioned no spread at all). So every formats[] row stamps one wire.recipes entry per attested rung -- the checkpoint's own vocabulary, in the spelling a checkpoint's config already records per rung -- and the validator refuses a stamp that forgets a rung, names one the family does not attest, or carries a body/span/plane the route does not decode (tessera.serving.scheme.ROUTES, the table the loader itself gates on). A producer preflight compares its checkpoint's wire.recipes entry at that rung against the stamp and tells 'attested on these bytes' from 'attested on this rung'. The three stamps are the pinned wire (sigma null everywhere): the v5 BF16 receipt (docs/measurements/tessera-bf16-route-served-2026-09-02.md) and the earlier E2M1x2/E4M3 receipts all predate any reach term, so until the served A/B at R=7 (the #48 gate) re-cuts the attestation on reach-term bytes, the honest reading of the BF16 row is 'route attested at 1792; KL receipt on the pinned wire', and now the table says so itself. The route attestation stands across window-table changes -- the decoder takes the table off the ALPHABET plane and the same kernel decodes the new bytes -- which is why this is a stamp and not a re-attestation. ADDITIVE for a reader that reads keys by name and ignores the ones it does not know: every key a v7 reader read is byte-identical. It is a version bump, not a silent addition, for a reader that validates: a document without attested_wire is refused, which is what contract_version 8 says -- exactly as v4 did for activation_contract.

native_extensions: the libraries this plugin LOADS into a serving process, beside the routes it EXECUTES. The contract published what runs and nothing about what is resident, so a consumer that keys reproducibility on extension residency -- PrismaQuant's serve fingerprint, whose section 7.4 records that a KL is bit-identical inside one container session and drifts 4-8x across them, keyed on whether a lane's .so was resident -- had to mirror the basename into its own pin file. That is principle 14 read backwards: a claim about THIS runtime, maintained in the other repository, where nothing here could refuse it on drift. Until 2026-09-03 that pattern named no Tessera extension at all, so a serve running Tessera's own native span-2 decode fingerprinted identically to a stock serve -- the one lane whose whole point is a custom decoder was the one lane the identical-residency rule could not see. One entry today: the span-2 NVFP4 decoder. It is published as a module_name_prefix and a filename_glob, NOT as a basename, because there is no exact basename to publish -- ext.py JIT-builds the module under a name carrying a build-identity hash, so the library on disk is tessera_nvfp4_<identity>.so and a consumer matching an exact stem would match nothing. match names the rule a gate applies ('basename_fnmatch'), because prose that said 'this is a prefix' is exactly the kind of field principle 14 refuses. The prefix is the constant _load_locked itself passes to cpp_extension.load, and the validator refuses any block that is not tessera.serving.ext.NATIVE_EXTENSIONS, so the table is DERIVED from the load path rather than typed beside it; tests/test_serving_native_extensions.py walks the import graph from tessera.serving and refuses any JIT load site reachable from it that this table does not declare, which is what keeps the list from going quietly short. when_unavailable replaces the 'optional: true' the issue proposed, because optional conflates two facts and answers the wrong one: what a fingerprint needs is not 'absence is survivable' but WHICH serve ran instead, and that differs by residency -- resident substitutes tessera.stock.materialize_stock and stamps decoder 'torch_materialize_stock' on every route record, streamed refuses outright because that path decodes inside a traced forward. So an absent .so with a streamed route record is an impossible pair, which is a stronger check than a boolean allows. The routes gate on this block rather than on a mode comparison of their own (nvfp4_route -> ext.substitutes_when_unavailable), the same way loader_axes is checked against ROUTE_TP_AXES. tessera_window_gemv stays OUT: the criterion is that the library can be resident in a SERVING process, and nothing reachable from tessera.serving loads it -- verified by the import walk, not by reading, so the day a route wires the window GEMV in, the table goes red. ADDITIVE for a reader: a v5 or v6 reader ignores a new top-level key, and no value it already read has moved -- verified, not asserted: PrismaQuant's own contract_answer() over the v6 and v7 payloads is byte-identical.

fused_module: what a vLLM-fused module's roles must SHARE and what is free PER MEMBER, as a value a producer's group allocator reads instead of guessing (#37). The rate is per member. That was always true of the DECODERS -- fp8_route and bf16_route call prepare_window on each role's own body_bits/rates/window_bits and concatenate, nvfp4_route packs each role's own rate/arity/memory/half scalars into that role's row slice -- but nothing published it, and the only place it was written down was the sidecar, which carried ONE q256 per module and refused any member that disagreed with it. So the exporter grouped a fused module on (grid, q256) equality and passed a mixed-rung group through at source precision, while PrismaQuant's group knapsack (fold ON by default) allocates exactly such groups: two halves of one pipeline describing different sets. The sidecar now spells a mixed group as a per-role q256 list (sidecar_q256), every role's rung goes through the same reader-range gate the module's one rung used to, and each member is compared against its own declared rate at parse. ADDITIVE for readers: formats[], lane_eligibility, tensor_parallel, expert_parallel and quant_method are byte-identical to v5, so a v5 reader that ignores unknown top-level keys gets exactly the answers it got before; what it must NOT do is assume q256 is scalar, and a pre-v6 PLUGIN does not -- it refuses the list form rather than mis-reading it. mixed_rung_receipt is false: the relaxation is proven by a decode identity on a real Qwen3-0.6B q/k/v at rungs 1024/900/1200 (element-for-element against the same roles decoded alone and against tessera.decode.materialize_fp8/materialize_bf16), not by a vLLM serve, and no lane_eligibility cell moved. NVFP4 is unaffected in practice: TESSERA_E2M1_K2 publishes the single point 896, so every member of an NVFP4 group lands on one rung anyway and the gate that says so is the reader range, not a rule about groups.

TESSERA_BF16_K1 stops being unattested. v4 gave its formats[] row an activation_contract, which says what the route EXECUTES; this says a receipt COVERED it, and the two are different claims: attested_rungs_q256 [1792] (R=7, the rung the receipt served) and two sm_121 dense cells, decode and batch, both bf16_unquantized on torch.mm with the row scale as an fp32 epilogue. The receipt is docs/measurements/tessera-bf16-route-served-2026-09-02.md: four route censuses on the pinned image -- resident/eager, resident/compiled, streamed/eager, streamed/compiled -- each recording all 112 declared modules on the TESSERA_BF16 route with decoder torch_window in BOTH the prefill and the decode shape and zero problems, plus a served KL-vs-BF16 in both residency modes on the Qwen-tokenized n=8 x 512 corpus against the image-matched teacher, with the folded stock twin on vanilla vLLM as the control. route_status is backed_with_serve_flag because the residency is selected by TESSERA_SERVE_MODE and both values were served; qualification is device_qualified because the censuses ran on this GB10 (sm_121, capability [12, 1]), not on a table. Nothing wider is attested: one rung, one platform, dense structure only, no routed-MoE cell, and tensor_parallel.units still caps this family at max_world_size 1.

formats[] rows gain activation_contract: the A-side contract the route for that family EXECUTES, as a value a gate can read. It was published only on lane_eligibility cells, so a family with no cell yet -- exactly TESSERA_BF16_K1, whose v3 entry landed unattested -- published its activation contract in changelog PROSE and nowhere a gate could reach, which is the principle-14 failure that field exists to prevent: a consumer could not tell 'unquantised by design' from 'nobody filled it in'. PrismaQuant's lane preflight found it within the hour, deriving an executes glob for a family whose A side it could not price. The value is checked against tessera.serving.scheme.ROUTES[route]['activation_contract'] -- the dict the routes themselves dispatch on -- exactly as loader_axes is checked against ROUTE_TP_AXES, so the document and the code cannot drift; and every cell's activation_contract must equal its family's row, so the two places that carry it cannot disagree. The A side is a claim about execution, not about attestation: the row says what the decoder feeds the GEMM, the cell says a receipt covered it, and TESSERA_BF16_K1 now honestly publishes bf16_unquantized with attested_rungs_q256 still empty. ADDITIVE: a v3 reader ignores the new field, and the cells it already read are unchanged.

tensor_parallel.units[] gains loader_axes: per axis, what this build's LOADER does with a shard on it ('sharded' or 'refused', plus a prose reason a gate does not read). The seam that cuts a unit landed (tessera.layout.slice_unit + serving/sharding), and the plugin's config gate had gone on refusing every tensor_parallel_size > 1 with a message saying the cutter was not in the build -- narrower than the code and, by then, false. The gate is now keyed on the slicer's PRESENCE, and the per-axis refusal moved to create_weights where the axis is known: TESSERA_E4M3_K1 cuts both axes (the window body's L-bit pad IS state_{-1}), TESSERA_E2M1_K2 cuts columns only (its span-2 TCQ decoders supply state_{-1} = 0 themselves). max_world_size is UNCHANGED at 1 and keeps its meaning -- the largest world size a served receipt covers -- because no multi-rank serve has been run; raising it needs a two-rank serve with a per-rank census and a KL against the single-rank arm, not a passing unit test. The validator no longer refuses a world size above one with the claim that a sharded form needs per-rank wires: it does not, the artifact is TP-agnostic and the cut happens at load. ADDITIVE -- a v1 reader that reads max_world_size still gets 1, which is the conservative answer. Third family: TESSERA_BF16_K1, the scalar BF16 grid over the CHANNEL plane and the same window body the E4M3 family ships, decoded to a plain bf16 tile and served W16A16 through the stock BF16 GEMM (activation contract bf16_unquantized -- a value, because a gate must be able to tell 'unquantised by design' from 'nobody filled it in'). It exists because the E4M3 ALPHABET floors the window body at ~0.022 out-space from R=6 upward while the identical trellis over bf16 keeps halving at ~1.93x per bit, so above ~6 bpp an 8-bit tile has nothing left to buy. reader_rate_range_q256 is [256, 4096] continuous at step 1, DERIVED the way E4M3's was in v2 -- 25 candidate rungs (every integer rate 1..16 plus nine non-integer rungs of the kind a Bresenham schedule makes: 300, 777, 779, 1000, 1023, 1500, 2047, 2500, 4095) encoded and taken through the route's own load path, parse -> shard -> prepare including the element-for-element cross-check against tessera.decode.materialize_bf16 (experiments/bf16_reader_rate_range.py). 4096 is the grammar's shaped domain (code rate 1..16 over a 16-bit alphabet) and the sweep reaches it: the recipe widens the window table to max(14, rate) above R=14 rather than refusing, and L=15 and L=16 both load. The only candidate refused was q256=777 over 128 columns, and that is a GEOMETRY refusal ('it needs 9/2 columns at rate 4') not a rate one -- it loads at 512 columns, so it does not bound the range. attested_rungs_q256 is EMPTY and there is no lane_eligibility cell: no container receipt covers this family yet -- no served census and no served KL against the plain-BF16 twin the exporter writes -- so every BF16 rung resolves unattested, which is the honest status and not a refusal. A cell is added when a receipt exists. Additive: a v1/v2 reader that does not know this family simply does not match it. tensor_parallel gains a TESSERA_BF16_K1 unit with the same loader_axes as TESSERA_E4M3_K1 -- both cut, because the axis answer is a property of the window BODY (its L-bit pad IS state_{-1}) and this family ships that body over the same CHANNEL plane; its create_weights calls the same require_axis_supported gate. max_world_size is 1 like the others: no multi-rank serve has been run.

reader_rate_range_q256 now states what the DECODER accepts, measured by encoding a unit at each candidate rate and running it through the route's own load path; the plugin refuses a declared q256 outside it (it did not before, and an allocated checkpoint carrying seven unlisted rungs served with nothing refusing). E4M3 widened from [1024,1024] to [256,2048] continuous at step 1 -- the bound is the trellis grammar's shaped domain (code rate 1..8 over an 8-bit-native alphabet), not the rungs anyone had exported. E2M1x2 stays the single point 896, bounded BELOW by the native decoder (span-2 TCQ only; the sub-cap WINDOW body has no served decode) and ABOVE by the same grammar (rate 7 of arity-2 native 8). candidate_rungs_q256 renamed attested_rungs_q256 because it never was the decodable set and reading it as one is how the gap opened: it is the rungs a lane_eligibility cell attests. Added an explicit grid to each entry so a (route, grid) pair with no published range refuses rather than resolving to another entry's numbers. candidate_rungs_q256 is retained as a DEPRECATED ALIAS of attested_rungs_q256 -- same list, refused if it disagrees -- so this stays an ADDITIVE change that a v1 reader can still read, which is why the schema string does not move. It is dropped at schema v2.
First published contract: two dense families, four cells, TP1/EP0.
